subject: physical-education
essentialQuestion: What can movement say that words cannot?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of beat, tempo, and phrasing in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe locomotor and non-locomotor sequencing using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving composing an original short sequence; correct it and explain why.
Connect refining a sequence through self-review with movement as expression and as stress relief and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Compose, refine, and perform a short original movement sequence for an audience of one trusted adult, or describe and notate it in full if the learner prefers not to perform.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Sequences may be seated, small-range, hand-and-arm only, or built at any tempo. Notation, description, or storyboarding is an accepted alternative to performing.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
